questions.stem: Last month's LP bound came from OR-Tools' PDLP on one thread. This month's rerun used four threads on the same machine and inputs, and the digest changed. What does that show?

options.text: A different thread count is another configuration, held to tolerance
options.says: Right: PDLP's roundoff depends on its shard count, so 4 threads repeated itself but differed from 1 thread (1,536 against 1,472 iterations).

options.text: PDLP on four threads cannot repeat even its own runs bit for bit
options.says: The four-thread runs repeated each other exactly; they differ only from the one-thread run.

options.text: The inputs must have changed, since a CPU solver never varies
options.says: The inputs were the same; the thread count alone changed the bits.

options.text: The machine is faulty, since the same solver gave other bits
options.says: Nothing is faulty: a change of thread count changes the order of the sums, and so the roundoff.

origin.section: On the CPU, a Fixed Solver, Method and Thread Count Repeat Bit for Bit

questions.stem: A team reruns an LP with cuOpt's default settings and gets 1,000,038.0 where last week's run gave 1,000,007.04. Same machine, same inputs. What should change so that reruns repeat?

options.text: Run cuOpt twice and keep the answer the two runs agree on
options.says: Two runs of a race can agree by chance and differ next time; the winner is not fixed.

options.text: Record which method won, and keep the concurrent default
options.says: Recording the winner explains each answer, but the next race can have another winner and another value.

options.text: Move the solve to the CPU, since a GPU never repeats
options.says: GPU PDLP with its method set repeated bit for bit; the GPU is not the cause.

options.text: Set the method to PDLP instead of the concurrent default
options.says: Right: concurrent mode races PDLP, barrier and dual simplex, and PDLP alone repeated in every run measured.

origin.section: cuOpt's Concurrent Default Is a Race: Record Which Method Won

questions.stem: Two manifests both say highspy 1.14.0, but their LP results differ in their last digits. One solve ran on the CPU, the other on the GPU image. Which manifest field tells them apart?

options.text: The versions block's highspy field, since each image reports its own build
options.says: The CUDA build reports 1.14.0 too, the same string as the CPU wheel, so the version alone cannot tell the builds apart.

options.text: The solver block's device field, with the card's model and CUDA versions
options.says: Right: the device, with the card's model and CUDA versions, records where the solve ran.

options.text: The result block's time field, since the GPU image's run finished sooner
options.says: The manifest leaves out the clock, and a time is a fact about the load, not the device.

options.text: The machine block's host name field, naming the GPU image's machine
options.says: The manifest leaves out anything that names the machine; the device fields carry the card's model, not the machine.

origin.section: The Manifest Records the Device, the Method and the Tolerance
